input.question: Let P(z) be a homogeneous polynomial of degree 4 in C[z] whose Hessian matrix Hes P is nilpotent, so P is Hessian nilpotent. If Delta := sum_{i=1}^n D_i^2 is the Laplace operator on C[z], must the iterated Laplacians of the powers of P eventually vanish in the sense that Delta^m(P(z)^(m+1)) = 0 for all sufficiently large m?

original_paper.title: Some Properties of and Open Problems on Hessian Nilpotent Polynomials

rewritten_question: Let P(z1, ..., zn) be a homogeneous polynomial of degree 4 with complex coefficients. Call P Hessian nilpotent if its Hessian matrix, whose (i,j)-entry is the second partial derivative of P with respect to zi and zj, is nilpotent. Let Delta be the Laplace operator D1^2 + ... + Dn^2. Equivalently, for such a polynomial P, the condition of being Hessian nilpotent is the same as requiring Delta^m(P(z)^m) = 0 for every integer m at least 1. Must it then follow that, for all sufficiently large integers m, the m-fold iterated Laplacian of P(z)^(m+1) also vanishes, that is, Delta^m(P(z)^(m+1)) = 0 eventually?

paper_evidence.quote: We also propose some open problems for further study of these objects.
A polynomial or formal power series P(z) is said to be HN (Hessian nilpotent) if its Hessian matrix Hes P := ( ∂2P / ∂zi∂zj ) are nilpotent.
Conjecture 1.1. (Vanishing Conjecture) Let ∆ := Pn i=1 D2 i be the Laplace operator of C[z]. Then, for any HN polynomial P(z) (of homogeneous of degree d = 4), ∆mP m+1(z) = 0 when m >> 0.
Proposition 1.2. For any P(z) ∈ C[[z]] with o(P(z)) ≥ 2, the following statements are equivalent. (1) P(z) is HN. (2) ∆mP m = 0 for any m ≥ 1. (3) ∆mP m = 0 for any 1 ≤ m ≤ n.
